_description: Hunt definitions for the Tartaria-RPG bounty system. 2026-05-26 OTA-055 — all hunts refactored to one of two standardized templates: standard_7 (7-stage informant-driven hunts) or bait_switch_5 (5-stage urgent-pacing hunts). Each hunt carries difficultyTier + recommendedHp + recommendedWeaponRarity so the player can read the danger before they accept. See app/engine/hunts.ts for the type definitions.

hunts.title: The Bog Dragon of Old Drakova
hunts.posterText: Drakovan reeve seeks proof of death — a long-shadow has been seen over the Mud Seas at dawn. Wing-mark longer than a barn. 800 TC on confirmed kill.

stages.narration: The Drakovan reeve closes the bounty book. "I don't know where it roosts. Old Mira does — out on the marsh edge. She lost half her cattle to it. Bring her this token, she'll talk."
stages.arbiter: "Posters in this country mean someone is desperate or someone has died," the Arbiter says. "Read the room before you sign."

stages.narration: Half a day toward Mira's holding, a wing-shadow crosses you. You crest the next rise and find what it left — a goat torn open, three obsidian-edged scales steaming in the silt. The Dragon knows there are eyes here now.

Mira reads the reeve's token and waves you to sit. "I'll mark his roost," she says. "But my boy went into the flooded shrine after the first attack. He's in there. Bring me back his locket. Then we talk."
stages.arbiter: "She has been carrying that wait for a season," the Arbiter says quietly. "Make it count."

stages.narration: The flooded shrine is silt-glass and old prayer. You find the boy where he fell, a Bog Wraith feeding on what's left. You drive it off and free the locket from his hand. It's still warm to the touch.
Mira reads the locket without crying. "Cathedral steeple. Deeper marsh. Go now." As you push out, a flock of lesser Wing-Things rises from the reeds — the Dragon's brood, sent to thin you.

On the locket's inside lid, scratched in a child's hand: a name. ESHREN. Mira's voice behind you: "He named it. He thought naming it would make it leave us alone." Speaking a Dragon's true name binds it for one breath. That is the breath you will use.
stages.arbiter: "One word, one moment," the Arbiter says. "Don't waste either."

stages.narration: You wade out to the cathedral steeple. The Dragon uncoils. You speak its name — ESHREN — and it stalls, for one long breath, eyes wide. Now or never.
stages.arbiter: "Whatever you do, do not let it get airborne again," the Arbiter says.

hunts.title: The Mud Titan of the Endless Stair
hunts.posterText: True Tartarian agent in the Outskirts wants a Mud Titan put down. It is collapsing the descent to a buried capital. 600 TC and reputation with the enclave.

stages.narration: The True Tartarian agent doesn't sit. "We can't go down there ourselves — every shake brings the Stair down on whoever's mid-descent. Find Master Karin in the upper concourse. She was the lead engineer when the Stair was still a stair. She'll know where it's resting."
stages.arbiter: "They never ask quietly," the Arbiter says. "They ask only when it is bad."

stages.narration: Half a day from Karin's office, the ground hammers under you. Two Reclaimers and a True Tartarian engineer are pinned under a collapsed gantry, calling for help. The Titan, far below, has woken something else. You dig fast.
stages.arbiter: "Other people's catastrophe is part of yours now," the Arbiter says. "This is the work."

stages.narration: Karin hears you out, then folds her arms. "I'll mark its patrol — I designed those landings, I know where it'll plant itself. But my old blueprints are sealed in the second-level archive. The lock's me-and-only-me. Bring them up. Then we plan."

You drop two levels into the buried archive. The seals open to your hand at Karin's word. As you pull the blueprint tube, a clutch of Mud Wraiths peels off the wall behind you — the Titan's vibration woke them weeks ago. You clear them.

Karin spreads the blueprints flat and circles a niche on the sixth landing. "There. It rests where the old core-conduit pools heat. Go now — every hour you wait, more Stair falls." Halfway down, a pre-flood Sentinel husk lurches awake on a landing — its loyalty programming hasn't decided whose side you're on yet.

On the fifth landing, a Sentinel power core sits in its cradle, still hot. Karin's blueprints show a chokepoint two flights down where a rigged core, dropped from the rail, will blast a wall onto the Titan's head. Wire it. Set it. Don't drop it.
stages.arbiter: "That core's a one-shot," the Arbiter says. "Place it where the Titan has to come."

stages.narration: You bait the Titan onto the chokepoint. The core drops. Half the wall comes with it. The Titan lives — mostly — and turns to you. Now finish.
stages.arbiter: "That bought you one limb of it," the Arbiter says. "The rest is yours."

hunts.title: The Sludge Behemoth at the Cradle of Dusk
hunts.posterText: Reclaimers Guild Speaker offers 500 TC for the head of a Behemoth that has begun crushing dive-camps near the Cradle. No fewer than four crews missing in a fortnight.
hunts.targetLocationName: the Cradle of Dusk (Behemoth's feeding pool)

stages.narration: The Reclaimers Guild Speaker pushes a sealed tube across the table. "Coordinates to Jarn. Old dive-master. He survived the last attack — only one who did. He'll tell you where the Behemoth feeds. Or he won't. Either way, he's the only mouth open on this."
stages.arbiter: "Survivors talk on their own terms," the Arbiter says. "Bring patience."

stages.narration: On the road to Jarn you cross a half-drowned camp. Three dive-tubes torn open. One man still breathing, ribs broken, calling for water. A Mud Crab the size of a pony hesitates at the edge of the camp, deciding between you and him. You decide first.
stages.arbiter: "Patch him before you ask anything," the Arbiter says. "Then ask."

stages.narration: Jarn won't look up from the rope he's mending. "I lost my harpoon-rig with the crew. Down in the wreck of the Marlin, half a league east. Bring it up and I'll mark your map. Otherwise we have nothing to talk about."

You dive into the Marlin's half-sunk hull. The harpoon-rig is wedged under the rib of the ship, where Jarn's crew went down with it. They didn't all stay dead — three Drowned Reclaimers turn at the sound of your tank. You clear them and recover the rig.

Jarn marks a pool on the chart with a black thumb. "There. It comes up to feed at the slack tide." Heading out, a chorus of Mud Sirens — drawn by the Behemoth's resonance — converges on your skiff. They sing. You commit.

Jarn shows you how to charge the harpoon-rig with an Aether Crystal. "This is the only thing that punches the silt-hide. Don't waste the shot — you get one before the rig burns out." You load the crystal. The rig hums in your hands.
stages.arbiter: "One shot to root it," the Arbiter says. "Then it's a knife fight underwater."

stages.narration: You wait at the slack tide. The Behemoth breaches. You fire the harpoon-rig. The crystal punches through silt-hide and the Behemoth screams — rooted in place, furious. Get in the water and finish it.
stages.arbiter: "The rig will burn out before it dies," the Arbiter says. "Don't be on the wrong end when it does."

hunts.title: The Iron Titan in the Sentinel Ward
hunts.posterText: Forgotten Order requests the deactivation of an Iron Titan still patrolling a Sentinel Ward. Order scholars cannot enter their target archive. 1000 TC. Order standing.

stages.narration: The Order envoy taps a sealed reliquary box twice and slides it across. "Brother Ammon. Cloister of the Closed Hand. He keeps the old Sentinel Ward maps. He'll give them to you when he sees this. Do not open the box."
stages.arbiter: "The Order's couriers do not say more than they have to," the Arbiter says. "Take the silence as instruction."

stages.narration: You cross a Sentinel patrol on the road — three units, lesser, still on a thousand-year-old loyalty loop. The truce between the Order and the Sentinels is paper. They challenge you. Fight or fade past.
stages.arbiter: "They will not pursue past their patrol arc," the Arbiter says. "Either disengage or end them quickly."

stages.narration: Brother Ammon opens the reliquary. Whatever's in it changes his face. "I'll give you the bypass codes. But the Ward's patrol log is in a half-buried relay tower a day east of here. Bring it. The codes are no use if the Titan has gone dormant."

The relay tower leans hard west, half-buried in silt. You climb to the operations room. An Order Apostate is in the doorway — left his faith and stayed for the relics. He won't let you pass with the log. You take it from him.

Ammon reads the log and his hand goes flat on the table. "It is still walking. Inner archive, third gallery. Go now." As you approach the Ward, drones lift from concealed cradles — automated defenses, two thousand years patient.
The inner door is keyed to Order blood. Ammon pressed his signet ring into your palm before you left — "the door knows me; let it know you through this." Lift the ring to the seal. The Ward opens.
stages.arbiter: "He gave you the only one he had," the Arbiter says. "That ring is the only key into the Order's inner rite."

stages.narration: The inner archive is colder than the Ward outside. The Iron Titan is at the far wall, head bowed in some ancient liturgy. It hears you enter. It rises. It is taller than the chamber meant for it.
stages.arbiter: "It does not tire," the Arbiter says. "Make every hit matter."

hunts.title: The Siren Queen of Zharak's Teeth
hunts.posterText: Drifters and Reclaimers alike have lost crews to the spires of Zharak's Teeth — a Mud Siren Queen leads the song. Anyone who silences her can keep what they salvage. 700 TC posted by a wandering drifter.

stages.narration: The drifter presses the poster into your hand and points east. "Her chorus just took another crew — pinned them between the south spires this morning. She'll move at dusk. Go now or there's no point going at all."
stages.arbiter: "That's a real bounty in your hand," the Arbiter says. "And no time to read it twice. Move."

stages.narration: Zharak's Teeth crest the water exactly as you were told. You wade in between the south spires expecting the Queen. The Queen is gone. Three lesser Sirens uncoil from the wreckage instead, calm and ready. The crew the drifter mentioned were the bait, not the prize. So are you.
stages.arbiter: "The Queen knew you were coming," the Arbiter says. "She prefers her hunts begun by her, not by you."

stages.narration: You sift the wreckage after the Sirens go quiet. A Reclaimer's broken survey-pen — the Queen's true spire is marked on it, three pillars north of where you stood. She moved the moment she heard your skiff.

You wade north spire-by-spire. Every pillar carries another Siren in waiting. The chorus rises around you — half song, half scream. You hold your line and push through, blade or breath, whatever it takes.
stages.arbiter: "If you stop moving, the song takes you," the Arbiter says. "Do not stop moving."

stages.narration: You break into the central pillar's clearing. The Queen sits on her mud-glass throne, calm and almost amused. "You should not have come," she says, low and warm. "But since you have — sing, or die quiet." The standing Sirens turn now, all of them, all toward you.
stages.arbiter: "She means it," the Arbiter says. "Neither option works in your favour."

hunts.title: Silence the Doubter
hunts.posterText: The Servants of the Giants name a Reaver who walks the Outskirts speaking against the Giants' return. The Servants do not raise their hand against him — they ask a hand that isn't theirs to. 150 TC posted at any Servants shrine.
hunts.targetLocationName: the Tartarian Outskirts (the Reaver's ridge camp)

stages.narration: The Servants priest bows just enough. "His last camp is two days west of the shrine. He moves at dawn — if you start now, you take him before he does. We do not raise our hand against him; you raise yours, and we will remember."
stages.arbiter: "They give you a clean path and clean hands," the Arbiter says. "Their preferred shape of the work."

stages.narration: You make the camp by dusk. Embers still warm. Reaver gone. Three of his sworn followers — Tartarian raiders, jaw-marked — rise from positions they'd set hours ago. He left them for you, the way another man leaves a note.
stages.arbiter: "He saw you coming a day off," the Arbiter says. "Cut through these and move."

stages.narration: You search the camp's debris. A boot-track heading due north, fresh. A Reaver's spiral-mark scratched into a stone — his next staging-ground, named in raider sign. He wanted the right kind of hunter to follow.

North through scrub and broken stone. Two more raiders strike from cover at the half-mile mark — they're not trying to stop you, only slow you. By the time you put them down, the Reaver has had another hour to set the meeting.
stages.arbiter: "He chose the ground," the Arbiter says. "Now you decide what to do with it."

stages.narration: The Reaver is on the ridge, alone, watching you climb. He doesn't draw until you crest it. "The Giants will rise," he says, almost gentle. "You are a small thing to send against that." Then his blade comes up.
stages.arbiter: "He has done this before," the Arbiter says. "So have you. Show him which of you means it."

hunts.title: The Boiler of Zharak's Teeth
hunts.posterText: Zharak's Teeth caravan-masters seek proof of death — a Steam Walker gone rogue is scalding the pass shut. Wing of steam seen a mile off. 900 TC on confirmed kill.

stages.narration: The caravan-master jabs the pass on his map. "Something old woke in the rocks and now it boils anyone who tries the Teeth. My drovers won't go. A wheelwright named Ost saw it — find him at the low camp, he'll point you up."
stages.arbiter: "A machine that has forgotten it is a machine is the most dangerous thing in this country," the Arbiter says. "It does not hate you. It simply does its old work on your body."

stages.narration: Half a day up the Teeth you find the pass fused — sand turned to glass in a long scalded stripe, and at the end of it a drover cooked in his boots. The Steam Walker knows the pass is watched now. It is waiting further up.

Ost the wheelwright will talk, for a price: his apprentice ran up the Teeth after the beast and hasn't come down. "Bring me the boy, or what's left," he says, "and I'll draw you the vent it roosts in."

You find the apprentice pinned in a scree-slip, leg broken, alive by luck the Walker passed him for dead. A Rust Lurker has come to finish what the mountain started. You drive it off and carry the boy down.
Ost keeps his word and marks the vent. As you climb, the pass itself turns on you — the Walker vents a scalding cloud down the chute, and lesser steam-things stir in the rocks, roused by the heat.

At the vent you understand it: the Walker is bleeding a cracked core, venting to keep from bursting. It cannot stop. Kill the venting and you kill the machine — but the moment you close the valve it will have one last, total breath to spend.
stages.arbiter: "It is dying and does not know it," the Arbiter says. "That makes it neither safe nor merciful. Mind the last breath."

stages.narration: You reach the roost as the Walker turns, core screaming, and vents everything it has left in one white blast. Close the valve and end it — or be the next stripe of glass in the pass.
stages.arbiter: "One breath," the Arbiter says. "Do not be standing in it."

hunts.title: The Serpent Under the Sinking Cathedral
hunts.posterText: Salvagers working the Sinking Cathedral want a Silt Serpent dead before it takes another diver. Longer than a barge, they say. 850 TC on confirmed kill.

stages.narration: The dive-boss counts three lost this season. "It nests where the Cathedral's nave floods deepest. My last diver, Wren, mapped its runs before it took her line. Her sister keeps the logbook — get it, and you'll know where it sleeps."
stages.arbiter: "The drowned keep their secrets in ledgers here," the Arbiter says. "Read the dead's careful notes. They paid for them."

stages.narration: The nave takes a hand of water an hour. In the shallows you find Wren's cut line and, tangled in it, a shed length of Silt Serpent skin the width of a door. It is bigger than the boss admitted. It knows the water is being read.
Wren's sister will trade the logbook for a promise: recover Wren's body from the flooded transept so she can be burned properly. "I can't bury a line and a boot," she says. "Bring her up."
You dive the transept and find Wren where the Serpent left her, and a Bog Wraith risen from the drowned to guard the drowned. You put it back down and bring Wren up into the light.

The logbook maps the Serpent's runs like a tide-chart. As you push toward the deep nave, the water around you thickens — the Serpent's silt-brood, a boil of young things sent to blind and slow you before the mother strikes.

Wren's last page holds the trick: the Serpent hunts by the pulse of Aether, and the Cathedral's old font still hums with it. Foul the font and the beast goes deaf and blind — for one dive's length, no more.
stages.arbiter: "Take its senses and it is only length and hunger," the Arbiter says. "That is still a great deal of both."

stages.narration: You foul the font and the deep nave goes silent. The Silt Serpent comes anyway, blind and furious, threshing the flooded dark. Now — while it cannot find you — or never.
stages.arbiter: "It is deaf, not gone," the Arbiter says. "Strike sure and strike once."

hunts.title: The Shade of the Endless Stair
hunts.posterText: Pilgrims on the Endless Stair are vanishing between one landing and the next. A Shifting Shade walks the steps. 950 TC on proof of its end.

stages.narration: The stair-warden has stopped counting the missing. "They go up whole and come down never. A Shade lives in the turns where the light can't reach. An old climber, Bael, survived it once — he keeps the shrine at the third landing. He'll know the pattern."
stages.arbiter: "A thing that lives where the light bends," the Arbiter says. "Then bring your own light, and doubt every shadow that is your own."

stages.narration: On the ascent you find a pilgrim's lantern still burning on an empty landing, its owner gone without a mark. The Shade takes cleanly. It has already noticed the lantern you carry.

Bael will share what he learned, but the Shade left him blind in one eye and afraid of the dark. "Sit the night vigil with me at the shrine," he asks. "I can't face the turning of the light alone. Do that, and I'll teach you to walk the Stair."
In the small hours a lesser dark tests the shrine — an Aetheric Apparition drawn by Bael's fear. You hold the vigil and put it down, and Bael sleeps through the dawn for the first time in a year.

Bael teaches you the Shade's law: it cannot cross its own cast shadow. As you climb to bait it, the Stair itself seems to lengthen — the Shade folding the light, throwing false landings and forked dark to lose you in the turns.

You understand it now. The Shade is a person the buried city swallowed, unmade into moving dark. Name it back for one breath and its edges hold still enough to strike. Bael gives you the name he heard it whisper: KESSA.
stages.arbiter: "It was someone," the Arbiter says. "Kessa. Say it kindly if you can. Then end it, kindly or not."

stages.narration: On the high turn where no light reaches, the Shade unfolds. You speak — KESSA — and for one breath the dark holds a woman's shape, still and startled. That breath is the only one you get.
stages.arbiter: "Now," the Arbiter says. "Before it forgets its name again."

hunts.title: The Siren of Drowned Drakova
hunts.posterText: Drakova's ferrymen won't cross after dusk — a Mud Siren sings the crossing and the crossers walk into the Mud Seas. 800 TC to silence it.

stages.narration: The head ferryman won't meet your eye. "It sings my brother's voice some nights. My wife's, others. Whoever it takes, it learns. A netter named Halla plugged her ears with wax and lived to see it — she's on the far quay, if she'll speak."
stages.arbiter: "It does not lure you with a monster's voice," the Arbiter says. "It lures you with a loved one's. Decide now, in the quiet, that you will not answer."

stages.narration: At the dusk crossing you find a fresh trail of boots walking straight off the quay into the silt, unhurried, glad. The Siren sang someone home an hour ago. It hears your oar and goes quiet — learning your sound.

Halla trades the wax-trick for a burial: her brother answered the song last spring and lies out in the shallows unclaimed. "Bring him to dry ground," she says. "I'll not have him be part of its choir."
You wade the shallows for Halla's brother and find a Bog Creeper has claimed the body for its own larder. You drive it off and carry the man to dry ground, out of the Siren's reach at last.

Halla seals your ears with netter's wax and the song goes flat and far. As you pole toward the roost, the Mud Seas churn — the Siren, unable to sing you down, sends the drowned it has already taken to pull you under by hand.

Deaf to the song, you can see the trick of it: the Siren has no voice of its own. It steals throats. Its own reed-throat is the one thing it cannot replace — foul it and the choir falls silent for good.
stages.arbiter: "Silence is the only mercy it will accept," the Arbiter says. "Give it. And give the coast its nights back."

stages.narration: You reach the reed-choked roost and the Siren opens a hundred stolen throats at once — soundless to your waxed ears, a gaping, furious quiet. Foul the reed and end the song. It has sung its last name.
stages.arbiter: "You cannot hear it," the Arbiter says. "Good. Do not learn to."

hunts.title: The Weaver of the Obsidian Pillars
hunts.posterText: Reclaimer salvagers at the Obsidian Pillars keep losing crews to an Iron Spider that webs the ruins in living wire. 750 TC on confirmed kill.

stages.narration: The salvage-boss shows you a coil of wire fine as hair and strong as cable. "It spins the old Tartarian filament into webs and my crews walk into them in the dark. A scavenger called Pike mapped the Pillars before it took his legs. Talk to Pike."
stages.arbiter: "It builds with the empire's own thread," the Arbiter says. "An honest thief. Do not admire it long enough to join the web."

stages.narration: Among the Pillars you find a crew's worth of tools scattered under a canopy of iron web, their owners gone but for the wire-marks. The Spider watches from a high pillar. It has already measured you for a strand.

Pike, legless and bitter, will draw the web-map for a bottle and a promise: his partner is cocooned somewhere in the Pillars and may yet live. "Cut him down," Pike says. "I can't climb to him. You can."
You find Pike's partner wound in iron silk, alive and half-mad, and an Aetheric Spider brood already feeding at the cocoon's edge. You clear them and cut the man free into the light.

Pike's map shows the Spider's core-web strung between the three tallest Pillars. As you climb to it, the ruins sing with tension — the Weaver plucking its own strands to shake you loose from a hundred feet up.
At the core-web you see the flaw: the Spider anchors everything to one master-strand humming with stolen Aether. Cut that and the whole cathedral of wire — and the Weaver on it — comes down at once.
stages.arbiter: "One thread holds the whole design," the Arbiter says. "Find it. Then do not be under the rest when it falls."

stages.narration: You reach the master-strand as the Iron Spider rushes down its own web toward you, fast as a dropped stone. Cut the thread and take it — or ride the collapse into the Pillars' teeth.
stages.arbiter: "Now, and then move," the Arbiter says.

hunts.title: The Apparition in the Red Tower
hunts.posterText: The Forgotten Order will pay well to lay to rest an Aetheric Apparition haunting the Red Tower of Nimari — it wears the faces of the Order's own lost scholars. 1100 TC.

stages.narration: The Order archivist is grey with grief. "We sent scholars into the Red Tower to read the cursed core's casing. They did not come back — and now something up there wears their faces and calls in their voices. Vesryn kept their field-notes. Start there."
stages.arbiter: "It will speak with the voices of people you might have saved," the Arbiter says. "It did not save them. Neither could you. Do not let it argue otherwise."

stages.narration: In the Tower's lower archive you find the scholars' abandoned notes and, pressed in a ledger, a rubbing of the core-casing that should not exist intact. The Apparition drifts a floor above, trying on a dead woman's laugh.
Vesryn will surrender the field-notes on one condition: recover the body of the lead scholar, his student, so she can be named and mourned. "I sent her in," he says. "Let me at least bring her home."
You find the student where the Tower's cursed Aether caught her, and a Shifting Shade circling what remains. You put the Shade down and carry her out, and Vesryn covers his face.

The notes reveal it: the Apparition is the cursed core's spillover, a wound in the Aether wearing whatever grief it finds. As you climb to the casing, the Tower turns hostile — the dead scholars' faces surrounding you, all speaking your failures at once.

At the casing you understand the binding: the Apparition is anchored to the intact core-shell the scholars died reading. Break the shell's seal and the wound closes — but every face it wears will scream at once as it goes.
stages.arbiter: "They are not really in there," the Arbiter says. "But it will sound exactly as if they are. Break it anyway."

stages.narration: You reach the core-casing and the Apparition wears every lost face at once, a chorus of the Order's dead pleading in one voice. Break the seal and lay them to rest — or add your own face to its collection.
stages.arbiter: "Do not answer them," the Arbiter says. "Only end it."

hunts.title: The Harpy of the Cradle of Dusk
hunts.posterText: Wayfarers at the Cradle of Dusk are being snatched from the road at twilight. A Mud Harpy nests in the dead spires. 850 TC on confirmed kill.

stages.narration: The road-warden points at the sky. "It takes them at dusk — that hour when the eye can't tell bird from shadow. A trapper named Ferel lost his daughter to it and lived. He hunts it still, out past the dead spires. Find him."
stages.arbiter: "It hunts the one hour you cannot see it," the Arbiter says. "Then do not trust your eyes at dusk. Trust the wind and the weight of the air."

stages.narration: At the road's edge you find a snatched traveler's pack, dropped from a height, and three grey pinions the length of your arm. The Harpy circled back to watch you find them. It is curious now, which is worse.

Ferel will guide you to the nest for one thing: his daughter's body, taken to the high spire two seasons past. "I can't make the climb," he says. "You can. Bring her down. Then I'll take you to the roost."
You climb to where the Harpy caches its kills and find Ferel's daughter among older bones, an Aetheric Raven flock already picking the site. You scatter them and bring her down to her father's arms.
Ferel leads you to the roost at last. As you close, the dusk erupts — the Harpy's brood, half-grown and screaming, flung at you to blind and slow you before the mother folds her wings and drops.

Ferel gives you the trick that saved him: the Harpy is deaf in a dive, all eyes, committed to the fall. Stand where the last light throws your shadow long and it will misjudge the strike by a hand — the only hand you get.
stages.arbiter: "It cannot pull up once it commits," the Arbiter says. "Be a foot to the left of where it aims. One foot."

stages.narration: At full dark the Harpy climbs, then folds and drops — a stone with talons. You hold your ground in the last light, let it commit, and step. Now, in the half-beat it cannot correct, end it.
stages.arbiter: "Do not flinch early," the Arbiter says. "The flinch is what it hunts."

hunts.title: The Fiend in the Tartary Dust
hunts.posterText: Caravans crossing the Great Tartary Plains are found scoured to bone, no tracks but the wind's. A Dust Fiend rides the storms. 900 TC on confirmed kill.

stages.narration: The caravan-mother spits grit. "It comes in the wall of dust and leaves the wind its plate. My outriders won't cross the deep plains now. A storm-reader called Yenna knows when it walks — she keeps the last well. Ask her."
stages.arbiter: "It hides inside the weather," the Arbiter says. "So learn the weather. On the plains the sky is the only warning you will get."

stages.narration: You find a scoured caravan half-buried — meat gone, metal frosted to glass where the Fiend passed. In the lee of a wheel, one survivor's scratched warning: IT TURNS WITH THE WIND. The Fiend rides the storm's own edge.

Yenna reads storms for the last well's water-price. She'll read this one for you if you clear the drowned pump-works below her well — something has fouled it, and a dry well on the plains is a slow grave. "Fix my water," she says, "and I'll give you the sky."
You descend Yenna's pump-works and find the foulness: a Bog Creeper denned in the cistern, breeding in the dark. You clear it and the well runs clean, and Yenna's hard face softens by a degree.

Yenna reads the coming storm and names the hour. As the dust-wall rises you ride out to meet it — and the Fiend, sensing a hunter in its weather, throws the whole plain's grit at you at once, a scouring dark that flays and blinds.

Yenna's last gift is the Fiend's law: it is only whole inside the storm; on still air it comes apart. Read the storm's eye — the one pocket of calm it cannot enter — and fight it from there, where it must hold together to reach you.
stages.arbiter: "Stand in the quiet at the heart of the storm," the Arbiter says. "It cannot follow you into the calm without falling to pieces. Make it try."

stages.narration: You reach the storm's eye and hold the calm. The Dust Fiend rages at the edge, unable to enter without unmaking, forced to lunge through the still air in a shape it can barely keep. That lunge is the whole fight. Take it.
stages.arbiter: "In the calm it is mortal," the Arbiter says. "Do not step back into the wind."

hunts.title: The Warden of Thametan's Tower
hunts.posterText: Stone Builders surveying Thametan's Tower woke something in its foundations — a Mud Golem that will let no one climb. 1000 TC on confirmed kill.

stages.narration: The lodge-surveyor nurses a broken arm. "We only wanted to read the Tower. Something in the footing stood up — a Golem, old as the stone, and it will not let us past the second floor. My apprentice Del stayed behind, trapped above it. Get to him."
stages.arbiter: "It is not angry," the Arbiter says. "It is doing its last order, a thousand years late. That makes it no less able to break you across a wall."

stages.narration: You reach the Tower's second floor and find the Golem's work: a stair collapsed to deny the climb, and Builder tools scattered where men ran. High above, a voice — Del, alive, walled in by rubble the Golem itself placed to keep him from the top.

Del calls down the deal through the stone: the Tower's upper chamber holds the treatise the Builders came for, but the Golem guards it. "Bring the reading down and I'll show you the Golem's seam," he says. "I watched it move for a day. I know where it's soft."

You climb past the Golem to the upper chamber and find the treatise — and an Iron Spider nesting in the Builders' abandoned gear, guarding it by accident. You clear the nest and take the reading down to Del.

Del reads you the Golem's seam in exchange for the treatise. As you descend to face it, the Tower answers — the Golem tearing its own stair apart to bury you, flinging the Tower at you a block at a time.

Del's watching pays out: the Golem's core-heart sits behind a plate that opens only when it winds up a full swing. Bait the swing, and for one beat the seam is bare. Miss the beat and the swing is the last thing you feel.
stages.arbiter: "It opens itself only to strike," the Arbiter says. "Its attack is its one weakness. Trade the risk for the opening."

stages.narration: You goad the Golem into a full overhead swing and the core-plate yawns. The Tower holds its breath. Drive into the seam now — or wear the blow that opened it.
stages.arbiter: "On the wind-up," the Arbiter says. "Not before. Not after."

hunts.title: The Plague Moth of the Sunken Enclave
hunts.posterText: A wasting sickness spreads from the Sunken Enclave's upper vaults. A Plague Moth breeds in the dark, dusting the air with rot. URGENT — 1100 TC.

stages.narration: A physician grabs your sleeve. "There's no time for the usual dance. Whole quarters near the Sunken Enclave are wasting — a Moth in the upper vaults, dusting the air with rot. Every hour it lives, another street coughs. Go NOW. Kill it at the source."
stages.arbiter: "No informant, no favor, no ritual," the Arbiter says. "Only speed. Some monsters you do not study. You outrun their spread and end them. Move."

stages.narration: You reach the vault you were sent to and the Moth is already dead — someone got here first, a salvager who cracked it open and is dying of the dust for their trouble. But the vault is a hatchery. This was one of many. The real brood is deeper.

The dying salvager gasps the truth: the Moth you were sent for was a drone. The queen roosts in the flooded reliquary below, and every drone she throws off doubles the sickness. You read her descent by the trail of rot-dust settling on the water.

The reliquary approach is a gauntlet of her drones, throwing themselves into your torch to blind it, dusting your every breath with rot as you push toward the queen's roost. You hold your air and cut through the swarm.
The Plague Queen fills the flooded reliquary, wings the width of the vault, the whole city's wasting breeding under her. Every second she lives is a street. End her, and end the plague at its throat.
stages.arbiter: "Everything she has thrown off dies when she does," the Arbiter says. "This is the source. There is no second chance and no time to be clever. Kill her."

hunts.title: The Alpha of Yuldra-Tul
hunts.posterText: A Mud Hound pack has taken the Yuldra-Tul road and their Alpha is smart enough to bait travelers into the pack. URGENT — 800 TC on the Alpha's head.

stages.narration: The Yuldra-Tul reeve is out of patience. "No time for tracking. The pack owns the road and the Alpha's clever — it fakes a lone lame hound to draw folk in, then the pack takes them. Cut the head off and the rest scatter. Ride out and do it."
stages.arbiter: "A clever predator is only a predator that has learned your habits," the Arbiter says. "So do not have habits today. Go, and do the thing it will not expect."

stages.narration: You take the road and find the bait exactly as warned — a lone hound feigning a broken leg. But when you close, the pack does not spring. The Alpha is testing whether you know the trick. It watches from the ridge, reconsidering you.

You read the Alpha's real game in the sign: it does not lead the pack, it herds prey toward a box canyon where the pack waits. It has been funneling the whole road into one killing ground. You find the canyon mouth by the bones.

You turn the trap — walk the canyon on your terms and the pack commits, pouring in expecting easy meat and finding a hunter. The Alpha throws the whole pack at you at once to overwhelm what its cleverness could not fool.

With the pack thinned the Alpha finally enters the fight itself — no more games, all teeth and grim intelligence, knowing that when it falls the rest run. Take its head and give the road back to the living.
stages.arbiter: "Kill the mind and the mouths scatter," the Arbiter says. "It knows that too. That is why it stayed on the ridge until now. It is out of ridge. Finish it."

hunts.title: The Salamander Under Voronov
hunts.posterText: Voronov's underworks are heating — an Aetheric Salamander has denned in a live Tartarian conduit and the whole quarter above may cook. URGENT — 1050 TC.

stages.narration: A Voronov engineer wipes soot and sweat. "No time to be thorough — the underworks are climbing past what the stone can hold. A Salamander's denned in a live conduit and it's feeding on the flow, getting hotter. If it doesn't stop, the quarter above bakes. Get down there."
stages.arbiter: "It is not just a beast, it is a rising temperature," the Arbiter says. "Every minute you spend planning, the ceiling of a city gets warmer. Go."

stages.narration: You reach the conduit the engineer marked and the Salamander is gone — moved deeper, chasing hotter flow, leaving the first conduit cracked and venting. It is not defending a den. It is following the heat toward the main line. So must you.

You trace it by the glowing conduit-scars to the main junction under Voronov's heart. Here it means to nest for good, wrapped around the quarter's primary Aether-line — the one that, if it bursts, takes the district with it.
The junction is a furnace of the Salamander's making, the air itself scalding, lesser fire-things spawned from the overheating flow lunging from every vent as you push to the main line.

The Aetheric Salamander coils the main conduit, glowing white, the whole quarter's heat cycling through its body. Kill it here, at the line, before it nests — or read Voronov's obituary in the rising glow.
stages.arbiter: "It is one conduit away from cooking a district," the Arbiter says. "There is no clever finish. Put it out at the main line, now, and let the city cool."
